I find a really difficult scenario to run in any RPG is an investigation. Balancing giving over the clues with keeping a mysterious atmosphere is mind meltingly hard. In a recent CoC game I ran 'The horror on Haldon hill. I found that the game was pretty rail roady. If you leave a trail of crumbs for the investigators to follow how do you ensure that they keep their own agency? They follow the clues and end up where you want them. I think perhaps the easiest solution to this problem is to provide lots of information, allowing the players to decide where they go, this is much easier to do in a campaign rather than a one shot, but they should always have the option of throwing a spanner in the works. How do you as GMs make sure your players have options?

In the CoC game I just ran the players were eventually saying 'well I guess there's nothing else to do except wait until the full moon.' Maybe they are just inexperienced players, but I feel like the fault may have also been mine.

All my other GM experience comes from Pathfinder which is a very different system and my comfort with it maybe makes it easier for me to improvise.
